threads.body: The test casts `future` to `FutureInternal` without first asserting it implements that interface. If Vert.x ever changes the empty-batch return type, this would fail with a `ClassCastException` instead of a clear assertion failure. Add an `isInstanceOf(FutureInternal.class)` assertion before the cast (similar to the Promise check).

replies.body:
Fixed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/612afad1936794245151aead09dcb123e8902585.

Added an explicit FutureInternal type assertion before the cast.

threads.body: Batch instrumentation still starts a span for empty request lists (and for non-4.0.x will also wrap the returned Future). This contradicts the PR goal of skipping instrumentation for empty batches and exporting no span. Consider short-circuiting in start() when requests.isEmpty() so the original Future is returned unchanged and no span is created.

replies.body: No code change needed. The PR now intentionally captures empty batches as PIPELINE spans. I updated the title and description to document synchronous span ending for Vert.x Redis 4.0.0 through 4.0.3 and normal asynchronous completion starting with 4.1.0.Beta1.

threads.body: This regression test currently asserts that an empty batch produces a PIPELINE span. The PR description says empty batches should skip instrumentation and export no span. The assertion should be updated to validate that no traces/spans are exported for emptyBatch().

replies.body: No code change needed. The PIPELINE span assertion is intentional. I updated the PR title and description, which still described the superseded no-span approach and caused this mismatch.
